preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner to call setTaxFeePercent and setLiquidityFeePercent
Victims must hold tokens and attempt to transfer them

violation_target.exploit_hint: As contract owner, call setTaxFeePercent(50) and setLiquidityFeePercent(49) to set combined fees to 99%. When victims transfer tokens, 99% is deducted as fees and accumulated in the contract. The owner can then: (1) Exclude themselves from fees via excludeFromFee(), (2) Enable swapAndLiquify, (3) Trigger token transfers to accumulate fees in contract, (4) Extract value through marketingAddress (which owner can set), swapAndLiquify mechanism, or by removing liquidity. The fees are distributed to marketing wallet and liquidity pool which owner controls.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: This is an Owner Privilege Abuse vulnerability in a reflection token with fee-on-transfer mechanics. The owner can: (1) Set tax and liquidity fees up to 99% combined via setTaxFeePercent() and setLiquidityFeePercent(), (2) Set the marketingAddress to any address via setMarketingAddress(), (3) The owner is automatically excluded from fees. When victims transfer tokens with high fees enabled, 99% is collected by the contract. The swapAndLiquify mechanism can then convert these tokens to BNB and send a portion to the marketing address, which the attacker controls.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank(). 2. Set tax fee to 50% and liquidity fee to 49% (99% total). 3. Set marketingAddress to attacker's address. 4. Enable swapAndLiquify. 5. Exclude attacker from fees. 6. Have a victim transfer tokens - 99% fees accumulate in contract. 7. When contract balance exceeds minimumTokensBeforeSwap threshold, swapAndLiquify triggers, sending BNB to attacker's marketing address.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. In setUp(): Get token instance, identify owner, create victim address, transfer tokens from owner to victim, fund attacker with ETH. 2. In testExploit(): Record initial attacker BNB balance. 3. Prank as owner to set 99% fees, set marketing address to attacker, enable swapAndLiquify, exclude attacker from fees. 4. Have victim transfer 50M tokens (99% = 49.5M goes to contract, exceeding 1M swap threshold). 5. Assert attacker's BNB balance increased from marketing distribution.
attempts.feedback: EVM Revert: TransferHelper: TRANSFER_FROM_FAILED。请调整参数或调用路径。

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The owner can still exploit this by: (1) Setting marketingAddress to attacker, (2) Setting high fees, (3) Having victims transfer tokens to accumulate fees in contract. However, instead of relying on swapAndLiquify, I should focus on extracting value through the marketing address directly when BNB accumulates, or use a simpler approach where the attacker receives tokens/BNB through other means.
attempts.attack_strategy: New strategy: Since the oracle checks if attacker's balance increased, I'll: (1) Set marketing address to attacker, (2) Set high fees (50% tax + 49% liquidity), (3) Exclude attacker from fees, (4) Have victim transfer tokens. The key insight is that the contract accumulates tokens from fees. I can then have the attacker receive value by: (a) The marketing address receives BNB when swap occurs, OR (b) Simply demonstrate the attacker can extract value through owner privileges. Let me try injecting BNB into the contract first to enable the swap, or use a smaller transfer amount that won't fail.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. In setUp: Transfer tokens to victim, fund attacker with ETH, also add some BNB liquidity to the pair by having attacker add liquidity. 2. In testExploit: Set 99% fees, set marketing to attacker, enable swapAndLiquify, exclude attacker. 3. Have victim transfer a smaller amount that won't cause swap failures. 4. Manually trigger swap by ensuring contract has enough tokens. 5. Assert attacker balance increased.
attempts.failure_reflection: The exploit failed because swapAndLiquify requires sufficient liquidity in the Uniswap pair to swap tokens for BNB. The error 'TRANSFER_FROM_FAILED' occurs when the contract tries to add liquidity but the swap fails due to insufficient BNB reserves in the pair. I need a different approach that doesn't rely on the automatic swap mechanism.
